label: first copy step (input = orig token 0, r/u/s/k/g) in long sequences
explanation: Sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). 85% of activation mass is at the first step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, input = the first original token fed back), concentrated in long sequences (L 8-9 hold ~88% of mass, none at L=3) and when the first token is r or u (~64% of mass), then s/k/g. Weak early-phase activity (~7% of mass) at original steps 3-8 and the delimiter step. The location is captured well (mass recall ~0.8), but even within that context only ~3% of steps fire; firing becomes more likely when the sequence has several u/i/j/2 tokens (precision up to ~13% with >=3 such tokens, at the cost of recall), so magnitude/selectivity depends on sequence content in a distributed way I could not pin down. Does not fire at t<3, at later copy steps (recall_idx >= 3 almost never), or on short sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=k (+3.42), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+3.33), orig0=u (+3.03), orig1=u (+2.81), phase=2 & in_tok=s (+2.75), phase=2 & in_tok=g (+2.67). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.31), orig_idx=-1 (-2.58), orig2=e (-2.47), orig3=f (-1.96).
